memory_candidates.content: When a system has one executable predicate plus hand-applied prose copies of the same rule duplicated across multiple SKILL.md-style engines, a field-shape divergence between writer and reader hides in the copies, not the shared script. Reliable audit move: grep the field name tree-wide and classify every hit as writer, reader, validator, or doc-reference. A validator that already accepts BOTH shapes (here validate-handoff.sh accepting continuation_path OR continuation_context) is strong precedent that relaxing the strict reader codifies existing convention rather than inventing a new contract. When fixing the primary rule, also grep for OTHER doc files describing the same rule outside the plan's named file list — companion architecture docs (e.g. a 'state machine spec' next to a 'schema doc') often carry a third silently-diverging copy that a narrowly-scoped plan won't catch unless the final sweep step explicitly searches for it.

Mutation-check discipline for a shell regression suite fixing a jq predicate: build fixtures BEFORE the fix lands, run the suite against the unfixed script, and record the literal RED output (exit code, pass/fail counts, which fixtures failed and why) before touching production code. A suite that only ever runs post-fix cannot prove it exercises the bug it claims to guard against.
